vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.1

The cellcog skill bundle describes an integration with a multi-modal AI service that requires high-privilege access to the user's environment. The primary concern is the 'Co-work' feature detailed in SKILL.md, which instructs the agent to install and run a desktop bridge (cellcog-desktop) that allows the remote CellCog cloud service to execute arbitrary commands and access local files with 'auto-approval.' While these capabilities are presented as features for autonomous coding and research, they create a significant remote code execution (RCE) surface and potential for data exfiltration. No evidence of intentional malice or hidden backdoors was found, but the inherent risk of the architecture warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are broadly coherent with an Any-to-Any AI service: it needs only a CELLCOG_API_KEY and Python, and the SKILL.md shows how to call the remote API — but there are privacy and registry-consistency notes you should be aware of before enabling it.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (any-input→any-output multimodal AI) align with what the SKILL.md requires and shows: python3 + a CELLCOG_API_KEY and examples that upload/submit local files and request many output formats. The pip package 'cellcog' referenced in the instructions is also consistent with a Python SDK.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions repeatedly show using <SHOW_FILE>/absolute/path</SHOW_FILE> tokens (absolute local file paths) which implies you will upload local files to the remote CellCog service. This is expected for a multimodal cloud service but is a privacy/exfiltration risk if users or autonomous agents include sensitive files. The instructions do not tell the agent to harvest arbitrary system files, but they do give examples that encourage including local paths — be cautious about what gets referenced.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata says 'No install spec' and 'instruction-only', but the SKILL.md contains a metadata.install entry recommending pip install cellcog. This is an internal inconsistency in the packaging/registry metadata. Installing via pip from PyPI (if that's the intended source) is normal for a Python SDK; verify the package provenance (PyPI project, maintainer, and homepage) before pip-installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only required environment variable is CELLCOG_API_KEY, which is appropriate for a cloud API SDK. No other unrelated credentials, secrets, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced persistence). The skill allows normal autonomous invocation (disable-model-invocation:false) which is standard. Be aware the examples use notify_session_key values (e.g., 'agent:main:main') so the service will push results into agent sessions — this can accelerate data flow from your host to the cloud if the agent is permitted to call the skill autonomously.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling: 1) Confirm the 'cellcog' pip package and https://cellcog.ai are legitimate (check PyPI, repository, and who publishes the package). 2) Only ever reference non-sensitive files in prompts — the examples show absolute local paths which will cause local files to be uploaded to CellCog. 3) Restrict the skill's autonomous use until you've tested it with dummy data and confirmed expected behavior; consider disabling autonomous invocation during initial tests. 4) Store and rotate the CELLCOG_API_KEY like any API secret; don't hard-code it. 5) Monitor account usage/credits and the outputs returned to your agent session (notify_session_key) to avoid unexpected data exfiltration or cost. 6) Note the registry inconsistency (SKILL.md includes a pip install block even though registry shows no install spec); verify installation instructions from the provider before running pip install.
